page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, paired with 2.0 GB of system memory. The processor includes 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. It lacks local storage and bundled GPUs, and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring in the top 25%. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations show limitations. The stress-ng multi-core performance and Geekbench multi-core scores fall into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively, reflecting the low core count. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only small block cached bandwidth scoring in the bottom 10% at 125.99 GB/sec, and large block uncached read/write speeds registering in the bottom 25%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance provides a low-cost entry point for compute-focused workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation but have minimal memory requirements. The 1:1 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it unsuitable for memory-intensive applications or large-scale databases, as evidenced by poor database operation benchmarks. It is suited for lightweight, single-threaded compute tasks, basic text processing, or simple web serving workloads that do not demand high memory capacity or high-throughput multi-threaded execution.
